scope: Hyperspectral/multispectral LiDAR radiometric correction, waveform decomposition, feature selection and LiDAR-aided unmixing abstract follow-up

records.title: A feature selection method for multimodal multispectral LiDAR sensing
records.abstractLevel: OpenAlex公开摘要索引（二级摘要）
records.abstract: Optical remote sensing can observe reflectance, fluorescence, Raman, or depolarization, while LiDAR measures geometry from propagation delay. Multimodal multispectral (MM) LiDAR combines these capabilities but creates high-dimensional data and instrument-design challenges. This paper proposes MGSVM-FS, a multiclass group feature-selection algorithm using structural sparsity and an all-in-one support vector machine, together with a workflow for feature-selection evaluation and decisions. An experimental MM LiDAR system provides reflectance, distance, and degree of linear polarization in 28 ten-nanometer channels. On thirty specimens from four construction-relevant material classes, three spectral channels with all modalities achieve a mean-F1 of 100% in the small dataset; MGSVM-FS improves mean-F1 by up to 25% over random selection and outperforms two filter and embedded methods.

records.title: A Discriminative Tensor Representation Model for Feature Extraction and Classification of Multispectral LiDAR Data
records.abstractLevel: OpenAlex公开摘要索引（二级摘要）
records.abstract: Multispectral LiDAR enables fine-scale 3D land-cover classification from point clouds. This paper represents each point and its local neighborhood with a second-order tensor encoding spatial location, spectral information, and neighborhood geometric-spectral structure. A tensor manifold discriminant embedding (TMDE) extracts features by compacting intraclass distributions and separating different classes; an SVM then performs classification. Experiments on two real multispectral point-cloud datasets show significant accuracy improvements over state-of-the-art methods.

records.title: A Novel Dynamic Warping Fusion (DWF) Method for Full-Waveform Hyperspectral LiDAR Signal Correction and Decomposition
records.abstractLevel: OpenAlex公开摘要索引（二级摘要）
records.abstract: Full-waveform hyperspectral LiDAR provides multichannel echo signals containing geometric and spectral information, but optical systems introduce interchannel time delays and response heterogeneity. The Dynamic Warping Fusion (DWF) method uses derivative dynamic time warping to align channels and synthesize a panchromatic waveform, then inverse alignment generates channel-specific initialization parameters for decomposition. Simulated data show R2 greater than 0.97 and RMSE below 0.24; the synthesized band has mean relative neighbor distance error below 2.51%. On measured data, DWF reduces this error from 5.11% to 2.27% versus MIWD, and integrated waveform areas produce spectra closer to the true spectrum than peak intensities.

records.title: A Novel Algorithm for Leaf Incidence Angle Effect Correction of Hyperspectral LiDAR
records.abstractLevel: OpenAlex公开摘要索引（二级摘要）
records.abstract: Hyperspectral LiDAR is affected by incidence-angle effects that limit quantitative applications. This paper combines Lambert and Beckmann laws to model complex surface reflection, includes wavelength and incidence angle in surface roughness and diffuse-fraction modeling, and derives a physically based correction for intensity and reflectance. Experiments with 30 leaves from three broadleaf species show improved intensity and reflectance consistency after correction. The algorithm is designed as a general approach for removing incidence-angle effects from hyperspectral LiDAR data.

records.title: Multichannel Interconnection Decomposition for Hyperspectral LiDAR Waveforms Detected From Over 500 m
records.abstractLevel: OpenAlex公开摘要索引（二级摘要）
records.abstract: Full-waveform hyperspectral LiDAR reveals target geometry and vertical spectral information, but channel-dependent reflectance and uneven laser energy make weak channels difficult to decompose at long range. This paper proposes multichannel interconnection decomposition (MIWD) to improve distance and spectral parameter extraction from hyperspectral waveforms. Experiments at about 518 m detect a whiteboard and green and yellow leaves, improving ranging and spectral detection over the best single channel. For two targets 60 cm apart, adding waveform channels raises the extraction success rate from 47% to 73%.

records.title: Design and Evaluation of Multispectral LiDAR for the Recovery of Arboreal Parameters
records.abstractLevel: OpenAlex公开摘要索引（二级摘要）
records.abstract: Multispectral LiDAR can recover structural and physiological information from trees. This paper designs and evaluates a prototype system for measuring leaf and bark area and abundance profiles on living conifers viewed from above. Because complete inversion is ill posed with four wavelengths, laboratory leaf and bark spectra constrain an extended reversible-jump Markov-chain Monte Carlo inversion. A separate experiment directly recovers a normalized difference vegetation index profile, verified against laboratory spectra. The results demonstrate potential for structural and physiological retrieval and fine spatial resolution using time-correlated single-photon counting.

records.title: Hyperspectral Image Unmixing With LiDAR Data-Aided Spatial Regularization
records.abstractLevel: OpenAlex公开摘要索引（二级摘要）
records.abstract: Spatially regularized spectral unmixing can oversmooth abundance maps and lose edges, while hyperspectral-derived edges may be corrupted by noise or illumination. This paper incorporates external LiDAR data into spatial regularization so that geometric edges guide unmixing. Evaluation on two simulated datasets and a real hyperspectral image shows better abundance estimates than hyperspectral-only spatial information, with substantial improvements for shadow-affected pixels.

records.title: Illumination Invariant Hyperspectral Image Unmixing Based on a Digital Surface Model
records.abstractLevel: OpenAlex公开摘要索引（二级摘要）
records.abstract: This paper proposes illumination-invariant spectral unmixing (IISU), using radiance hyperspectral data and a LiDAR-derived digital surface model to explain illumination and shadow variability physically. Incident angles, sky factors, and sun visibility from the DSM model endmember variability and are optimized with a straightforward solver. Compared with existing methods, IISU estimates more accurate abundances and shadow-compensated reflectance, especially in shaded pixels.

records.title: Multichannel Weak Signal Extraction Based on Multispectral LiDAR
records.abstractLevel: OpenAlex公开摘要索引（二级摘要）
records.abstract: Weak echoes are common in full-waveform LiDAR and reduce detection and extraction accuracy. This paper proposes multispectral LiDAR weak-signal extraction (MSL-WSE), evaluated with measurements from a multispectral LiDAR system. Correlation coefficient, RMSE, and effective extraction rate show that MSL-WSE detects and extracts weak echo parameters accurately, supporting more realistic and fine-grained true-color 3D point clouds.
